title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.
comment: 27 pages, 10 figures, 10 tables. Submitted to ACM Transactions on Quantum Computing

bite.hook: New trapped-ion instruction set runs quantum simulations 10x faster by packing more data into each individual ion.
tldr: Researchers developed a hardware-native instruction set for hybrid qudit-oscillator systems in trapped-ion quantum processors.
They mapped electronic manifolds directly to single-ion qudits, allowing local intra-ion transitions instead of multi-ion operations.
Simulations of a three-chromophore complex ran 10x faster than previous qubit-based methods with 1.1% error.
bite.whyItMatters: Scaling quantum computers is hard because adding more ions introduces noise and complexity. This approach does more with fewer ions, making quantum simulations of chemistry significantly more efficient.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to build a complex machine using only simple light switches (qubits). This team figured out how to use a 'smart switch' (qudit) that can be set to many different positions at once, allowing them to do the same work with far fewer parts.

glossary.shortDef: A quantum unit of information that can exist in more than two states, unlike a binary qubit.
glossary.eli5Def: If a qubit is a light switch that is either on or off, a qudit is like a dimmer switch that can be set to many different levels.

glossary.shortDef: A mathematical technique used to break down complex quantum time-evolution into smaller, manageable steps.
glossary.eli5Def: Think of it like taking a long movie and breaking it into individual frames so you can process them one by one.

glossary.shortDef: The study of how electronic and vibrational energy states interact within a molecule.
glossary.eli5Def: Looking at how a molecule's electrons move and how the whole molecule wiggles at the same time.
